annotations.text:
Waiting room, three directions.

All three use the live app's tokens exactly: #0a0b0e / #121319 / #1b1d25 surfaces, #262932 borders, #ffb454 accent, Inter + JetBrains Mono, 3px radii, the room's own 44px top bar.

The question each answers differently: what fills the screen while you decide which seat to take.

A — Seat rail + schedule ribbon

Seats run left to right in draft order along the top; picking one opens what that seat actually buys: all 16 picks drawn on the draft's own 224-pick axis, so the WAIT between them is visible. Seat 1 and seat 14 look obviously different here.

Trade-off: the ribbon is a new object nobody has seen before, and 14 seats in a rail get narrow.

B — Room list + seat detail

The room as a scannable list (draft order down), the seat under consideration at full size on the right, every round spelled out. Densest of the three and the most familiar shape.

Trade-off: two columns of numbers, no picture — the difference between seat 5 and seat 6 is something you read rather than see.

C — Full board

The draft room's own snake board, empty: seats across, rounds down, the pick number in every cell. Nothing new to learn, and it is literally the screen you are about to be looking at.

Trade-off: 224 cells of equal weight, so the seat decision has to be found in it rather than handed to you. Closest to what is built today.
